summary: Round 2, test review. All five round-1 items were re-measured in a private tree rather than accepted, and all five hold: T1's named mutation (`if (hop.from() > 0) return;`) now fails theDELTASAfterTheCheckpointAreReplayed with 12 vs 10 -- the K=5/12 tail is genuinely two deltas deep; T2's 'probe but ignore the answer' mutation now fails aPredecessorTOOSHORT at 102 vs the 30 bound (real value 26, unbounded 102, so the bound discriminates); T3's pair now kills BOTH off-by-ones -- `sequence()-2 > upTo` fails the barrier+2 test at 9999 vs 5, and `sequence()-1 >= upTo` fails the barrier+1 test at 27 vs 18; T4's isEqualTo(18L) is load-bearing and killed two mutants on its own; T5's noRenew() has replaced every LocalSequencer.sleepFor(RENEW) in both bounded suites (grep: zero remain). The split lost nothing -- the four correctness tests moved verbatim and the fenced-leader one got STRONGER (RA -> streamOfTerm(0), 9,999 -> a barrier computed from a RECOVERED CommitLog). LocalSequencerFailoverTest's four moved totals stayed EXACT equalities, GETs are still pinned at 18/46, both dimensions still pinned, and ADR-0035 states the numbers that moved. ONE NEW MAJOR: the T1 fix closes the crude mutation but not the boundary next to it -- the 12 commits all carry ONE stream, so only the LAST delta above the checkpoint is constrained, and two off-by-ones on the very line M4.9 added (`hop.from()`/`startAfter`) leave the whole 785-test suite green. Measured, with the concrete three-line fixture change that kills them. Three minors, none blocking.

findings.summary: theDELTASAfterTheCheckpointAreReplayed pins that the tail is not dropped WHOLESALE, but not where the tail STARTS. All twelve commits go to streamOfTerm(0), and offsets in a RunCommit are ABSOLUTE -- so reading only the LAST delta above the checkpoint already yields 12. Two boundary mutations on the exact line this task introduced survive the full suite: (a) ChainReplay.java:368 `keys.keyFor(hop.from() - 1)` -> `keys.keyFor(hop.from())`, and (b) ChainReplay.java:254 `new Hop(chainEpoch, checkpoint.sequence(), upTo)` -> `checkpoint.sequence() + 1`. Both measured: BUILD SUCCESSFUL, all tests green. This is the same defect class the fixture's own javadoc says was found at the TERM level ('with one shared stream a mutant that stopped the walk after the first ancestor PASSED') -- unfixed one level down, at the DELTA level, inside the test written to close it. Remedy measured in my tree: send commit i == 10 to streamOfTerm(1), assert streamOfTerm(0) is 11 and streamOfTerm(1) is 1. Unmutated: green. With mutation (a): FAILS with 'expected 1L but was 0L' -- the stream restarts at offset 0.
findings.failure_scenario: A leader checkpoints at sequence S and then commits deltas S, S+1 for streams X and Y respectively. A takeover replays from the checkpoint with an off-by-one in `startAfter`, so delta S is never GET at all. Stream X's offsets come only from delta S, so its nextOffset falls back to whatever the checkpoint carried and the new leader reassigns offsets X has already ACKED -- I2, and NFR-11 across a failover, silently, on the bounded path M5's 300 plugin nodes run. Every cost assertion stays green because the mutation issues FEWER requests, and every correctness assertion stays green because the one stream under test is also touched by the last delta.
findings.blocks_under: docs/internal/standards/review.md rules major-blocks and fixed-or-argued; testing.md rule 9 (a surviving mutant is killed or argued in baselines/mutants.txt) and rule 13. NOT evidence the commit is too big: the remedy is three lines inside a test this commit already adds, and no production change is implied.

findings.summary: The checkpoint probe added to the neverOpened branch IN THIS DELTA is executed but not constrained. Deleting the whole block (the probe and its break) leaves the full suite green -- measured, BUILD SUCCESSFUL. The branch itself IS reached: replacing it with a throw fails 8 existing tests (CommitLogCrossEpochTest x4, CommitProtocolSimulationTest x3, LocalSequencerFailoverTest x1), so this is testing.md rule 8's exact failure -- a line covered without being pinned. It is NOT an equivalent mutant: I built a 25-line T1 fixture (epoch 4 CONTINUEs to a sealed-at-0 epoch 3, epoch 2 entirely empty, epoch 1 carrying entries plus a LATEST checkpoint claiming 500) and it passes at 500 with the probe and fails at 100 without it. The sibling in-loop probe was round 1's T2 for exactly this reason and got a test; this one, added in the same delta, did not.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer refactoring ChainReplay deletes this block -- the javadoc beside it says it is unreachable today, which is a plausible argument FOR deleting it, the same shape as round 1's M4.9-R1-1. Nothing goes red. When M4.23 closes the burned-epoch gap, or any caller reaches replayAncestry without routing through firstInheritableAncestor, the crossing past a run of burned epochs is unbounded again -- O(all commit-log entries ever written), the regression this whole task exists to remove -- and no test says so.
findings.blocks_under: Not blocking. testing.md rule 8 / rule 9. Today's harm is a cost regression on a path guarded by an ordering invariant in LocalSequencer.start, and the comment beside the code states that honestly rather than claiming coverage it lacks. A backlog row or a commit-body line, or the fixture above.

findings.summary: The extraction did not happen. BoundedRecoveryFixture's class javadoc says 'The fixture M4.9's two bounded-recovery suites share', and grep says only BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest references it. LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest kept verbatim PRIVATE copies of PREFIX, TTL, RENEW, A, RA, TestClock, manager, frozen, noRenew, both request overloads and streamOfTerm (LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest.java:56-123), plus imports now unused there -- Body, Checkpoint, Checkpoint.StreamOffsets, IOException, each appearing exactly once, on its own import line. BoundedRecoveryFixture.java:98-107 also carries a dangling javadoc for a takeoverCost that is not in that file (the compiler already emits dangling-doc-comments for the same shape in FaultInjectingStore).
findings.failure_scenario: T5's fix -- freezing the renew ticker inside the counting window -- now exists as two independent copies of noRenew(). The next fixture-level correction lands in one and not the other, and the suite that missed it goes back to a real 3s ticker inside a measured window: a latent flake in a test whose whole value is an EXACT request count (isEqualTo(30L), isEqualTo(18L)). A reader who trusts the 'two suites share' sentence will also make that mistake by editing the wrong copy.
findings.blocks_under: Not blocking. No testing.md rule; the claim in the javadoc is simply false of the staged bytes, which this tree treats as worth recording. Deleting the sentence, or actually importing the fixture in the cost suite, are both one-line fixes -- and per review.md rounds guidance, fixing a minor now is permitted and usually wrong.

findings.summary: crossFromCheckpoint's `offsets.merge(key, at.nextOffset(), Math::max)` weakened to `offsets.put(key, at.nextOffset())` leaves the full suite green -- measured. Unlike T6 and T7 this one looks EQUIVALENT today: replayAncestry runs once per ChainReplay instance and every applyChain call happens AFTER the walk, so the offsets map is provably empty at every crossFromCheckpoint call site. Recorded not as a missing test but because the javadoc above it states a reason no test can distinguish from a no-op ('taking the later value unconditionally would rewind the stream (I2)'), which is the unpinned-rationale shape M4.8b2 and M4.8c each recorded three times.
findings.failure_scenario: A future change gives ChainReplay a second replayAncestry call on one instance, or moves an applyChain inside the walk. `put` then overwrites an already-merged higher offset with an older chain's lower one and rewinds a stream -- I2 -- and no test moves, because none ever reached this line with a non-empty map. The javadoc will still claim the merge is what prevents it.
findings.blocks_under: Not blocking, and NOT a demand for a test: an equivalent mutant cannot be killed. Either the line is T0-testable by making crossFromCheckpoint's precondition explicit, or the javadoc says the merge is defensive against a shape that cannot arise today, the way the neverOpened caveat does.

verified_not_findings: K=5 with 12 commits: the tail IS non-empty -- measured at exactly two deltas (checkpoints land at sequence 6 and 11; skipping the tail yields 10, not 12). The comment's claim that K=4 would empty it is consistent with that arithmetic.

aPredecessorTOOSHORT's isLessThanOrEqualTo(30L): real value 26, unbounded walk 102, one ancestor hop ~8.4 requests. The bound is meaningful and no single-hop regression fits in the 4 requests of slack. An unbounded walk does NOT satisfy it.

isEqualTo(18L) is what the code issues on the unmutated tree, and it is the only assertion that kills `sequence()-1 >= upTo` (27 vs 18) and the residual of `if (hop.from() > 0) return;` (17 vs 18). The hand-written checkpoint is written to `backing` BEFORE the CountingBinStore wraps it, so it is outside the counted window.

The split lost no assertion: all four correctness tests moved verbatim, and aCheckpointCoveringEntriesPASTTheBarrierIsNotUsed was strengthened on two axes (per-term stream, barrier computed from a RECOVERED CommitLog).

testing.md rules 4-5 on LocalSequencerFailoverTest: 28->30, 56->58, 20->22, 47->52 are budget MOVES, not assertion weakenings -- still exact equalities, GETs still exactly 18 and 46, both the per-entry and the per-ancestor dimensions still pinned, and ADR-0035 carries the numbers per cost.md R18.
Tier is right throughout: T1 on MemoryBinStore, no Thread.sleep, no fixed port, no system temp, fakes rather than mocks.
